title: The ALMA-CRISTAL survey: Widespread dust-obscured star formation in typical star-forming galaxies at z = 4─6
question: Investigate dust-obscured star formation activity and the spatial extent of dust emission in 26 normal, representative star-forming galaxies at z = 4–6, and examine distributions of the dust-obscured and unobscured star-forming regions.

data.angular_resolution: ~ 0.3'' (~ 1.9 kpc at z = 5); average natural-weighted beam 0.46'' (2.9 kpc)

what.value: Publicly available photometric catalog in COSMOS field (COSMOS2015 catalog) with 10 broad bands, 12 medium bands, and 4 Spitzer bands

evidence.quote: We cross-match positions of the CRISTAL galaxies to publicly available photometric catalogs in COSMOS (COSMOS2015 catalog, Laigle et al. 2016)
and 12 medium bands on Ground-based telescopes, and 4 _Spitzer_ bands that achieve the best sensitivities among the bands covering similar wavelength.

what.value: Publicly available photometric catalog in GOODS-S field (ASTRODEEP catalog) with 4 broad bands, 23 medium bands, 10 HST and 4 Spitzer bands

evidence.quote: and 23 medium bands on Ground-based telescopes, and 10 _HST_ and 4 _Spitzer_ bands on space telescopes from the ASTRODEEP catalog.

evidence.loc: Appendix A: CIGALE parameters used to estimate global properties
evidence.quote: We take 4 broad bands (U, B, R, K_s) and 23 medium bands on Ground-based telescopes, and 10 HST and 4 Spitzer bands on space telescopes from the ASTRODEEP catalog.

what.value: Best-fit FIR SED template and scaling factor (ν L_ν=158µm / L_IR = 0.133) for main-sequence galaxies at z = 4-6

evidence.quote: we use the best-fit FIR SED presented in Béthermin et al. (2017) to estimate the total IR (8–1000 µm) luminosities of the CRISTAL galaxies.

We calculate the total FIR luminosities of the CRISTAL galaxies by converting the measured dust continuum fluxes at the rest-frame 158 µm using a scaling factor described Béthermin et al. (2020, ν L_ν=158µm / L_IR = 0.133).

external_data.citation: Béthermin et al. 2017; Béthermin et al. 2020

what.value: Integrated [C II] spectral line profiles and central frequencies from the ALPINE survey

evidence.quote: We determine the spectral frequency coverages by centering [C II] frequency derived from the integrated [C II] spectral line profile in the ALPINE survey.

recipe.goal: Estimate galaxy-integrated stellar masses, SFR_SED, and L_UV via multi-wavelength SED fitting
recipe.method: Cross-match galaxy positions within 1'' to COSMOS2015 and ASTRODEEP catalogs and perform multi-wavelength SED fitting using CIGALE
key_parameters: Delayed-τ SFH: τ_main = [100, 300, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000] Myr; Age_main = 50 Myr steps in [50: 1000] Myr; τ_burst = [10, 50, 100] Myr; Age_burst = [10, 20, 50] Myr; f_burst = [0.0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2]
Metallicity Z = [0.2, 1] Z_⊙; Nebular log_10 U = -3.0, line width = 300 km s^-1; E(B-V) = 0.1 steps in [0.0: 2.0], E(B-V) factor = 0.44, R_v = 3.1
SFR_SED averaged over the last 100 Myr
assumptions: Bruzual & Charlot (2003) stellar population synthesis models, Chabrier (2003) IMF (0.1-100 M_⊙), Calzetti et al. (2000) dust attenuation law, flat universe with Ω_M = 0.3, Ω_Λ = 0.7, H_0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1

recipe.goal: Combine visibilities, image rest-frame 158 µm dust continuum, and measure flux densities and S/N
recipe.method: Concatenate visibilities with CASA/concat, exclude ±0.45 GHz around [C II] line, make dirty mfs continuum images (natural weighting and uv-tapered) without primary beam correction, pick peak flux within 0.5'' radius of [C II] position, and smooth 2.0''-tapered image to 3.0'' beam with imsmooth for total flux densities
key_parameters: uv taper scales: 0.25'', 0.5'', 1.0'', 2.0''; final smoothed beam: 3.0''; search aperture radius: 0.5''; RMS calculated with 3σ clipping where PB response is 0.5 to 0.9; detection threshold S/N >= 4
assumptions: Excluding ±0.45 GHz avoids broad [C II] line contamination (FWHM/2 ~ 250 km s^-1); 3.0'' beam includes all flux density within a single beam

recipe.goal: Measure effective radii of rest-frame 158 µm dust continuum in the visibility plane
recipe.method: Subtract continuum sources > 2'' away using CASA tclean (down to 1.5σ with 2'' masks) and uvsub; fit a 2D circular exponential disk profile (n = 1) directly to visibilities using UVMultifit
key_parameters: Sérsic index n = 1 (exponential profile), circular disk fixed axis ratio (q = 0 as written in text); two-component fitting when residual map shows second component with S/N > 10 (CRISTAL-22)
assumptions: Surface density profiles of dust continuum are represented by a circular exponential profile (n = 1)

recipe.goal: Derive total infrared luminosities (L_IR) and infrared surface densities (Σ_IR)
recipe.method: Convert rest-frame 158 µm dust continuum fluxes to total IR (8–1000 µm) luminosity using the scaling factor from Béthermin et al. (2020), and calculate Σ_IR = L_IR / (2π r_e,dust^2)
assumptions: Best-fit Draine & Li (2007) dust emission model from Béthermin et al. (2017) corresponding to modified blackbody with T_dust ~ 42 K

recipe.goal: Measure rest-frame UV effective radii from HST/WFC3 F160W images
recipe.method: Construct empirical PSF by stacking normalized, reprojected point sources; generate sigma maps from drizzle weights and mask maps from SExtractor segmentation maps; fit 2D Sérsic profile (fixed n = 1) using GALFIT and circularize radius via r_e,UV = r_e,UV^major * sqrt(q)
key_parameters: Point source selection: 2.0'' to 0.5'' aperture flux ratio in [1.2, 1.4], S/N > 7500, no neighbors within 3''; SExtractor: detect_minarea=5, detect_thresh=2, detect_nthresh=16, deblend_mincont=0.0001; GALFIT: Sérsic index n = 1 (axis ratio fixed to 1 if non-convergent)

recipe.goal: Calculate obscured fraction of star formation (f_obs) individually and via stacking in stellar mass bins, and evaluate correlations with galaxy properties
recipe.method: Compute f_obs = SFR_IR / (SFR_UV + SFR_IR) for individual galaxies and in 3 stellar mass bins via median image stacking of 3''-smoothed images scaled by (1+z)/d_L^2; compute Spearman rank correlation coefficients between Δf_obs and UV-dust spatial offset, size ratio, Σ_IR, and axis ratios
key_parameters: Stellar mass bins: log_10 M_* [M_⊙] = [9.3 : 9.8], [9.8: 10.2], [10.2: 10.9]; taper scale 2'', smoothed beam 3''; redshift scaling factor (1+z)/d_L^2
assumptions: Madau & Dickinson (2014) conversion from L_UV and L_IR to SFR_UV and SFR_IR; β_int = -2.41 for molecular index I_m

answer_key.quantity: Number of galaxies detected in rest-frame 158 µm dust continuum (S/N >= 4)

evidence.quote: Among 26 galaxies composed of 20 galaxies observed by the Cycle-8 ALMA Large Program, CRISTAL, and six galaxies from archival data, we have individually detected rest-frame 158µm dust continuum emission from 19 galaxies, nine of which are reported for the first time.

In a total of 26 extended CRISTAL samples (18 original CRISTAL targets, 6 CRISTAL+ galaxies, and 2 serendipitously detected galaxies in original CRISTAL fields), we found that 7, 8, and 11 galaxies have dust continuum emissions with S/N < 4, 4 <= S/N < 6.5, and S/N >= 6.5 respectively.

score_reason: The core analysis workflow (CIGALE SED parameters, continuum channel exclusion, tclean uv-tapering, UVMultifit exponential profile fitting, and GALFIT UV fitting) is well documented and uses standard tools, and Table 1 provides a rich numeric answer key. However, crucial target metadata (coordinates, redshifts, [C II] frequencies, ALPINE cross-IDs) and calibration details are deferred to companion papers in preparation.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA datasets are now public in the archive via the listed project codes, the visibility-fitting and tapered-imaging recipe is clear, and Table 1 provides exact per-target flux densities, L_IR, f_obs, and dust/UV effective radii to benchmark against once target cross-identifications are obtained.
